records.title: Engineers' Code of Ethics
records.text: Engineers shall hold paramount the safety, health, and welfare of the public in the performance of their professional duties. Engineers shall perform services only in their areas of competence Engineers shall issue public statements in an objective and truthful manner. Engineers shall act in professional matters for each employer or client as faithful agents or trustees, and shall avoid conflict of interest. Engineers shall build their professional reputation on the merit of their services and shall not compete unfarily with others. Engineers shall act in a manner as to uphold and enhance the honor, integrity, and dignity of the profession. Engineers shall continue their professional development throughout their careers and shall provide opportuities for the professional deelopment of those engineers under their supervision.

records.title: The Fundamental Principles
records.text: Engineers uphold and advance the integrity, honor, and dignity of the engineering profession by: Using their knoweledge and skill for the advancement of human welfare; Being honest, impartial, and serving with fidelity the public, their employers, and their clients; Striving to incrase the competence and presitge of the engineering profession; Supporting the professional and technical socities of their disciplines

records.title: External Vice President Committee (EVP)
records.text: The External Vice President's Committee focuses on projects that involve affiliates of the College of Engineering, including clubs, administrative groups, and external organizations. Projects include but are not limited to FMPI (the Free Menstual Product Initiative), the Blue and Gold Certification Program, and the expansion of ethics education to both faculty and students.

records.title: Technical Committee
records.text: The Technical Commitee is responsible for creating, managing, updating, and optimizing the ESC suite of applications and technology. The technical committee in the past has managed the following applications: Google Drive, Internal Website, ESC Website, and the ESC Email and Web Servers (Via the OCF). This year, we plan to continue updating this software and also develop new applications to be used by ESC.

records.title: Finance Committee (FiComm)
records.text: The Finance Committee is responsible for the disbursement of funds for Blue and Gold organizations. This is handled through the annual Initial Allocations process as well as year-round FiComm meetings, which give organizations a chance to request additional funds. In addition, FiComm strives to achieve a greater sense of community within the College of Engineering by organizing finance workshops and other related events.

records.title: Internal Vice President Committee (IVP)
records.text: The Internal Vice President’s Committee is centered around advocating for and supporting student organizations and the student body. In addition, the committee works to improve relationships between departments and students, focusing especially on initiatives related to equity, diversity, and inclusion.
records.keywords: exec officers president leadership board

records.title: Communications Committee
records.text: The Communications Committee is responsible for handling social media engagement and for maintaining relations with the ESS, the College of Engineering, and all Blue and Gold certified clubs. In addition, the committee is responsible for photography, videography and graphic designing for all events. Specific projects include: Sending out weekly newsletters to the engineering student body Managing the Universal Google Calendar Organizing “Day in a life of a Berkeley Engineer” and other Instagram series Recruiting new club members

records.title: Engineers' Week Committee (EWeek)
records.text: The Engineers' Week Committee plans one of the biggest events in the College of Engineering. The committee is tasked with working with ESC's corporate sponsors, partnering with Blue and Gold certified organizations, and working with the administration to host this weeklong event. Some of the events planned by the committee for 2020 were Engineers Ball and Engineering 4 Kids Day

records.title: Faculty Panel - COVID 19: Building More Ethical and Sustainable Solutions May 2019
records.text: Seven excellent Berkeley faculty members joined the Engineering Student Council to discuss how engineering innovations impact the fight against the COVID-19 pandemic. Faculty members shared their own research, which ranged from improving hospital ventilators to changing airport operations. Attendees included Professors of CEE Jasenka Rakas, Scott Moura, and Khalid Kadir; Professors of EECS Michel Maharbiz, Robert Pilawa-Podgurski, and Bin Yu; and Professor of ME and BioE Dorian Liepmann.

records.title: General Meeting - CalZoom: Case Studies of Current Times September 2020
records.text: For the first event of the academic year, the ESC wanted to address current events whose impact affects the community - three pressing issues were discussed: 1) Racism in Academia, 2) Political Participation in CoE, and 3) Accessibility and Student Advocacy During COVID-19. Participating students were split into these three groups and brainstormed solutions that could be enacted and applied to the College of Engineering. Dean Tsu-Jae Liu graciously joined the conversation and listened to student opinions.

records.title: Poll-ar Bears: A Voting Workshop September 2020
records.text: With 2020 being an important presidential election year, the Engineering Student Council created a workshop specifically highlighting the options for students to register and vote safely. The workshop’s topics included: why it’s important to vote, how to register in California, COVID-19 voting precautions, and where to find unbiased news sources.

records.title: Hack to School Workshop October 2020
records.text: Students have had to familiarize themselves with a new online environment this semester - this workshop introduced students to technical hacks and tips that could aid them in navigating their academic studies. Topics included: Gradescope, Google Calendar, Zoom, bCourses, etc.

records.text: Engineers Week (EWeek) is a weeklong event comprising of various professional, social, and design-build activities. Though primarily catered towards the 3,600+ undergraduate engineers on campus, each year EWeek reaches over 8,000 students from a variety of majors and degree programs, and that reach continues to grow. Our theme for this year is "World Carnival at Berkeley", and the celebration will occur from the Monday the 14th to Friday the 18th of February. Every day will feature two exciting events, all of which will earn you raffle tickets towards the end of EWeek giveaway. Prizes include an electric scooter, JBL speaker, Amazon gift cards, and more, so don’t miss out on the action! Keep scrolling for more information on the main events that you can look forward to! records.title: Q: What if I don’t know what engineering (on non-engineering) major I want to study?
records.text: A: There are many ways to learn about different majors and concentrations. Engineering Student Services (ESS) hosts an event every semester called “Major Madness” for students to talk to their peers and help them decide which major best suits their interests. Another way to learn more about different majors is to talk to upperclassmen in a major you are interested in exploring, or by talking to your advisor.
records.keywords: tutoring tutor academic study

records.title: Q: How do I know what classes to take?
records.text: A: A great resource to check out is the “Four Year Degree Plan” mapped out for each major. Make sure to keep track of the major, college, and campus requirements when deciding what classes to take each semester. The Berkeley Course Catalog has all courses listed for each semester and is a good way to learn more about different courses. There are also peer advisors at ESS to help answer any extra questions.

records.title: Q: Where do I find resources for advising and counseling?
records.text: A: Your ESS advisor can help you navigate degree and graduation requirements, academic procedures, and offer guidance and support. Each department also has advisors to help students with programs, facilities, and research opportunities. Peer advisors can give personal advice based on their perspective about topics like how to choose electives and juggling classes. Counseling and Psychological Services (CAPS) has an office in ESS and counselors are here to talk about any personal, professional, or academic concerns. There are walk-in hours, or you can schedule an appointment during the week. The Tang Center also offers counseling services.
records.keywords: mental wellness counseling therapy hear caps

records.title: Q: Where can I learn about the most recent internship, research, and scholarship opportunities?
records.text: A: The weekly ESS newsletter provides up to date information about important deadlines, workshops, and numerous opportunities. Your advisor or department may also have weekly emails/newsletters, so make sure to check your inbox for new information. Please email us at technical@esc.berkeley.edu for any questions you would like to see added onto this page.

records.text: Bears for Financial Success is a peer-to-peer financial wellness program housed in the Financial Aid and Scholarships Office at UC Berkeley. We offer workshops and one-on-one appointments to help students manage their personal finances in college and beyond.

records.title: Cost of Attendance Adjustment Request
records.text: Your financial aid eligibility is based on a standard cost of attendance, or student budget. We may be able to increase your budget—and your financial aid eligibility—if you incur expenses during the academic year that are higher than your standard financial aid budget. This is called a Cost of Attendance Adjustment Request. Please note that there is no COA Adjustment process for the summer term.

records.title: UC Berkeley Scholarship Connection
records.text: A surprising number of students fail to see that identifying scholarships can be one of the most important parts of the successful scholarship search. There are thousands and thousands of scholarships available to students through internet searches and scholarship guides, but no one student will every qualify for all of them. Even if one person were to qualify for all of them, though, most students at UC Berkeley probably don't have the time to apply for each and every one. For this reason, a well-defined scholarship search can be invaluable to students looking for some extra money to fund their education, research proposal, or community service project. The best and cheapest way to run a scholarship search is to find a good, reliable scholarship search engine (like UC Berkeley Scholarship Connection scholarship database.)

records.title: iGrad Finacial Aid Tool
records.text: iGrad Finacial Aid Tool begins with asking you to create a profile. Once your profile is created, you will have access to a personalized dashboard containing resources that will enable you to improve your money management, career, and student loan knowledge and skills. With recommended video tips, quick financial lessons, personalized job search and more, you will be well equipped to ensure your successful financial well-being in college and beyond.

records.text: Volunteer Income Tax Assistance (VITA) volunteers provide free, quality income tax preparation assistance for low and moderate income, elderly, disabled, and non-native English speaking individuals. records.title: CalFresh
records.text: CalFresh, also known as the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program SNAP, is an nutrition program that can help you stretch your monthly budget! CalFresh can provide eligible students with the ability to buy and eat nutritious and healthy foods! CalFresh benefits are pre-loaded monthly into an EBT card that can be used like a debit card at most major chain grocery stores, like Trader Joe’s, Safeway, and Costco. It can also be used at some smaller stores, like the Berkeley Student Food Collective!

records.title: Food Assistance Program
records.text: Food Assistance Program is for students who lack access to food in the short-term and are waiting for your CalFresh benefits, or are not eligible for CalFresh benefits, applying to the Food Assistance Program may be an option. Through the support of an additional funding source, we encourage all students who are experiencing food insecurity to review the Application for Additional Food Assistance on our Forms page.

records.title: UC Berkeley Food Pantry
records.text: UC Berkeley Food Pantry is a direct response to the need among the student and staff population for more resources to fight food insecurity––the lack of nutritious food. With rising fees, textbook costs, and living expenses, it has become increasingly difficult for students to juggle the costs of living with the costs of obtaining a university degree, and thus many students are finding themselves choosing between essentials such as food and the costs of college. The UC Berkeley Food Pantry was established to provide emergency relief to help students and staff at the University of California. It is a part of the campus-wide food security efforts.

records.title: Cal Nourish
records.text: Cal Nourish is a way for staff to come together to help Berkeley students who struggle to make ends meet during the winter curtailment. According to the UC Undergraduate Experience Survey, 1 in every 5 UC Berkeley students self-report having to “skip meals in order to save money.” Finding money for food over the holidays can be an especially tough challenge for an estimated 800 of these students.

records.title: First Thoughts
records.text: Initially, looking for housing can seem a bit daunting. Especially for many Berkeley students, this is the first experience they will have to find housing in Berkeley. As a first step, look for roommates. Since there are many different types of housing, having an agreement with your roommates is key to having a smooth living accommodation process. Once you have roommates, remember to keep calm! Finding housing can be hard especially when trying to work with other people. Compromises may need to be made but losing your calm should not be one of them. Below are the steps to get started.

records.title: Get Started
records.text: Step 1: Roomates Find people you want to live with (1-3 roomates recommended) Make it clear with your roommates that communication is key (if there are issues in the beginning with your roommates, then the apartment finding experience will be terrible) Step 2: Rooms: Recommended number of people to room with per living situtation (including yourself) Studio: 2 people max 1 Bedroom: 2-3 People max (3 is a tight fit) 2 Bedroom: 3-5 People max (5 people is a tight fit) 3+ Bedroom: Usally 2 people per bedroom Dorm style: 2-3 people Step 3: Distance Near Campus (5-10 min walk): Places close to campus are usally 1 Bedroom/Studio apartments Close but not near campus: Usally have 2-3 bedroom apartments avalible 3 is rare in new buildings unless there is a penthouse Step 4: Cost Set a limit to how much each person wants to pay Step 5: Necessities Prepare a list of potential amenities you guys would: a) Absolutely NEED (ie. Living Room) b) To make it comfortable (ie. Carpet Flooring) c) Would be nice to have (ie. In-unit Washer and Dryer) Step 6: Ask Around Ask upperclassmen friends (perferably graduating) if they're leaving their place Post on FB pages (check Step 8) Step 7: Bane of My…

records.title: Steps to get started with making!
records.text: Usually people that start out with using the makerspaces tend to focus on 3D printing and laser cutting since they are relatively easy to use compared to other machines such as a CNC. The great thing about attending UC Berkeley is the amount of support available at your disposal. If you have no idea how to use CAD (Computer Aided Design) such as Solidworks, go the fast route and find examples online. Look for examples that you can download as a .stl file. STL stands for stereolithography and is the standard format used by most 3D printing software such as CURA. Once you find a design/make a design and save it as a .stl file, use a compatible slicing software. If you are using a 3D printer that is part of a makerspace on campus, they will have a recommendation to which software to use. For instance the Type A 3D printers in Jacobs Hall use Cura Type A slicing software. Afterwards, save your file as gcode. GCode is sent to the 3D printers. Send the G-code to the printers

records.title: Getting Started Laser Cutting
records.text: Due to the dangers of laser cutting, we recommend that you are fully trained by a design specialist in the makerspaces. Laser cutting basically involves a powerful beam (laser) burning through a material such as wood. These devices need to be operated in an open and well-ventilated room. For further background information, check out this Instructables page!

records.title: Jacobs Institute for Design Innovation
records.text: The Jacobs Institute for Design Innovation is UC Berkeley’s interdisciplinary hub for learning and making at the intersection of design and technology. With a Maker Pass students can explore, prototype, and tinker in the Jacobs Hall Makerspace. The Jacobs Institute also offers a variety of resources to students interested in getting involved with design-focused student groups, in attending events, or in learning more about design opportunities through Jacobs' student services advisor. Sign up for the Jacobs Newsletter to get updates on events and news at the Jacobs Institute.

records.title: CITRIS and the Banatao Institute
records.text: The Center for Information Technology Research in the Interest of Society (CITRIS) and the Banatao Institute create information technology solutions for society’s most pressing challenges. CITRIS and Banatao support students from concept to prototype through a variety of programs and labs that bring together multiple disciplines to address critical challenges. Programs and labs include: CITRIS Invention Lab (requires Maker Pass) CITRIS Tech for Social Good CITRIS Foundry Startup Accelerator CITRIS Social Apps Lab Plus, check out a 3D Printer through CITRIS Invention Lan's GoFab(link is external) program. Open to all Maker Pass Holders, the Invention Lab is offering a suite of 3D printers that are available for checkout to extend your creativity and making outside of the lab, into your living room, dorm, kitchen, cafe, or personal workspace.

records.title: The Moffitt Makerspace
records.text: is a general access Makerspace located on the first floor of Moffitt Library. Operated primarily by student staff, the Makerspace features support for core maker activities such as CAD design, 3D printing, digital prototyping with digital components (e.g., Arduino, Raspberry Pi), as well as traditional craft and hand tool based design activities for wood and fabrics. It also offers training workshops to help and guide students learning both the basics (e.g. safety and basic use of equipment, use of software applications) and more advanced tutorials for projects and guided learning activities..

records.text: The mission of the Engineering Student Council is to represent the engineering student body; support engineering societies in reaching their full potential; and promote a diverse community through successful collaboration between students, faculty, societies, and the College of Engineering.

records.title: Engineers' Code of Ethics
records.text: Engineers shall hold paramount the safety, health, and welfare of the public in the performance of their professional duties. Engineers shall perform services only in their areas of competence Engineers shall issue public statements in an objective and truthful manner. Engineers shall act in professional matters for each employer or client as faithful agents or trustees, and shall avoid conflict of interest. Engineers shall build their professional reputation on the merit of their services and shall not compete unfarily with others. Engineers shall act in a manner as to uphold and enhance the honor, integrity, and dignity of the profession. Engineers shall continue their professional development throughout their careers and shall provide opportuities for the professional deelopment of those engineers under their supervision.

records.title: The Fundamental Principles
records.text: Engineers uphold and advance the integrity, honor, and dignity of the engineering profession by: Using their knoweledge and skill for the advancement of human welfare; Being honest, impartial, and serving with fidelity the public, their employers, and their clients; Striving to incrase the competence and presitge of the engineering profession; Supporting the professional and technical socities of their disciplines

records.title: What is Blue and Gold Certification?
records.text: Blue and Gold Certification is a process through which engineering student organizations at Berkeley demonstrate their commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion within their organizations. All certified organizations have attended several mandatory trainings, stripped exclusive requirements from their applications, and reflected on ways in which club culture at Berkeley can be improved for all students. In return, these organizations are given access to a wide range of benefits, including funding, publicity, and other resources.
records.keywords: blue gold b&g certification certified

records.title: Why are we doing this?
records.text: For years ESC has received complaints from students that the club culture at Berkeley is too exclusive and unwelcoming, a description that fundamentally opposes our understanding of the purpose of student organizations. As beneficiaries of campus resources paid for by tuition dollars, we believe that all organizations (including ourselves) have a responsibility to serve the student body. The purpose of Blue and Gold Certification is to reward groups who are already fulfilling this role and entice others to do the same.

records.title: The Process
records.text: All certified organizations have gone through an involved process to assure they are meeting the standards of the program. Some key requirements are listed below, but you can also check out this portal for more information about the process. Applications for the 2021-2022 school year have closed, but if your organization is still interested in becoming certified, we encourage you to check out our Development Program.

records.title: Sexual Violence & Harassment Training
records.text: Why This training enables student leaders to effectively prevent and respond to instances of sexual violence and harassement.

records.title: Equitable Strategies Training
records.text: Why Student leaders learn how to promote equality and inclusivity in their application process and their organization as a whole.

records.title: No GPA minimums / transcripts / resumes
records.text: Why Organizations should admit students based on interest and demonstrated commitment to the organization rather than prior experience.

records.title: Demographic Survey
records.text: Why This enables ESC to better understand the demographic of students who are joining Blue and Gold certified organizations.

records.title: Finance
records.text: ESC awards funding to certified organizations through Initial Allocations (spring) and Ficomm funding (periodically throughout the year). We generally have around $70,000 to award annually, so we encourage all eligible groups to apply!

records.title: Treasurer Training
records.text: All certified organizations are required to send their treasurers to one of our Treasurer Trainings every year, the purpose of which is to educate organizations on how they can apply for and spend funds granted by ESC. We have included the slides on our website for the convenience of those who attended.

records.title: Faculty Panel - COVID 19: Building More Ethical and Sustainable Solutions May 2019
records.text: Seven excellent Berkeley faculty members joined the Engineering Student Council to discuss how engineering innovations impact the fight against the COVID-19 pandemic. Faculty members shared their own research, which ranged from improving hospital ventilators to changing airport operations. Attendees included Professors of CEE Jasenka Rakas, Scott Moura, and Khalid Kadir; Professors of EECS Michel Maharbiz, Robert Pilawa-Podgurski, and Bin Yu; and Professor of ME and BioE Dorian Liepmann. “The faculty panel was a great experience! I was able to sit down with great professors and get to know them on a personal level rather than just a classroom setting and create connections” - Xochitl Ramos, class of 2022, mech E

records.title: General Meeting - CalZoom: Case Studies of Current Times September 2020
records.text: For the first event of the academic year, the ESC wanted to address current events whose impact affects the community - three pressing issues were discussed: 1) Racism in Academia, 2) Political Participation in CoE, and 3) Accessibility and Student Advocacy During COVID-19. Participating students were split into these three groups and brainstormed solutions that could be enacted and applied to the College of Engineering. Dean Tsu-Jae Liu graciously joined the conversation and listened to student opinions.

records.title: Poll-ar Bears: A Voting Workshop September 2020
records.text: With 2020 being an important presidential election year, the Engineering Student Council created a workshop specifically highlighting the options for students to register and vote safely. The workshop’s topics included: why it’s important to vote, how to register in California, COVID-19 voting precautions, and where to find unbiased news sources. "The Voting Workshop covered all the basic things we need to legally and rightfully voice our opinions. It was highly educational and even as an international student I feel like I've learned more about the country I am currently living in." - Belinda

records.title: Hack to School Workshop October 2020
records.text: Students have had to familiarize themselves with a new online environment this semester - this workshop introduced students to technical hacks and tips that could aid them in navigating their academic studies. Topics included: Gradescope, Google Calendar, Zoom, bCourses, etc.

records.title: Founded in 1974 as the Engineer's Joint Council
records.text: Our mission still reflects the original purpose of the EJC Since the Engineer's Joint Council founding, we have continually supported the engineering student body at Berkeley through advocating for students' rights within the Collge of Engineering, supporting over 85 engineering student organizations, and hosting events to bring together the engineering community. For over 30 years, ESC has been responsible for handling and disbursing ASUC funds to engineering student organizations. We also host one of the largest organization spaces on campus as well as one of the largest engineering themed events on campus, Engineer's Week. Next
